doc_hints.hint_excerpt: Resolve planning contradiction: 1. **Scored scheduler vs lexicographic schema lock.** Runtime docs define a scored ready-set; graph schemas still hard-code lexicographic node selection.

Resolve planning contradiction: 2. **Automation-first default vs HTE/visible/manual-default behavior.** `Run_Modes.md`, `newtools.md`, and several approval flows still assume interactive or visible execution as the normal baseline.
Resolve planning contradiction: 3. **Single Overseer vs package + seam overseers.** Runtime and UI docs still model one Overseer while the emerging design requires dual governance layers.

Resolve planning contradiction: 4. **Tier authority vs node/package/seam authority.** Tiers remain first-class in widgets, breadcrumbs, HITL boundaries, and state displays even where the graph is already treated as the canonical execution input.

Resolve planning contradiction: 5. **One project / one worktree / one current context vs multi-project, multi-worktree orchestration.** Several storage keys, UI assumptions, and auth flows still treat runtime context as singular.
Resolve planning contradiction: 6. **Legacy blocked payload fields vs normalized blocked-state contract.** Old and new field names coexist across Docker, runtime recovery, and policy docs.

Execute research follow-up: 1. **Define the dual-overseer runtime model canonically.** Lock package overseer vs seam overseer authority, spawning rules, corroboration/review responsibilities, and identity/model assignment.

Execute research follow-up: 2. **Design the package/seam/lane schema family.** Decide which objects are persisted canonically (`package`, `seam`, `lane`, `promotion`, `review`, `resolution_thread`) and which are projections only.

Execute research follow-up: 3. **Unify requested vs effective execution identity.** Extend the existing requested/effective Persona/model pattern to include account, lane/worktree, and overseer class.

Execute research follow-up: 4. **Specify package-based worktree lane pools.** Define lane ownership, pool sizing, contamination detection, safe-point restore behavior, and Source Control visibility for PM-owned worktrees.
